items.cite: Aaron Copland and Vivian Perlis, *The Complete Copland* (Pendragon Press, 2013).
items.note: Copland’s account of his decisions, teachers and collaborators. The two memoir volumes are brought together with Perlis’s commentary and a postlude on his last years.

items.cite: Howard Pollack, *Aaron Copland: The Life and Work of an Uncommon Man* (University of Illinois Press paperback edition, 2000; first published 1999).
items.note: A detailed study of the life and works, covering the private life, political commitments and individual compositions, with the context of the familiar ballets.

items.cite: Elizabeth B. Crist, *Music for the Common Man: Aaron Copland during the Depression and War* (Oxford University Press, 2005).
items.note: Crist connects the musical choices of El Salón México, the ballets and the wartime works with the left-wing cultural politics of the 1930s and 1940s, and asks whose America they represent.

items.cite: Annegret Fauser, *Aaron Copland’s Appalachian Spring* (Oxford University Press, 2017).
items.note: Traces how a wartime commission for Graham, Copland and Noguchi became an emblem of American life: the ballet’s making, choreography, performances and later meanings.

items.cite: Elizabeth Bergman Crist and Wayne D. Shirley, eds., *The Selected Correspondence of Aaron Copland* (Yale University Press, 2006).
items.note: Annotated letters record what Copland said at the time of composition, separately from his later memoirs.
